ProjectWeave request for the selected Task (data): {"task": {"id": "I_kwDOUDROfM8AAAABeiUuVQ", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4BlR_zzhIDWfM", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4BlR_z", "number": 309, "title": "Remove transient Web microphone toggle messages to prevent Graph Library layout shift", "body": "## Goal Remove unnecessary **transient progress messages** from the Graph Library **Web microphone** ON/OFF toggle so successful toggling does **not briefly shift the page layout**. Keep actionable failure/permission/compatibility guidance and the existing safe permission/consent flow. ## Observed behavior and current code The Graph Library renders `

` **between the header and the graph workspace** in [`extension/graph-library.html`](https://github.com/takahirox/my-audio-to-text/blob/main/extension/graph-library.html). It becomes visible when populated; [`extension/graph-library.css`](https://github.com/takahirox/my-audio-to-text/blob/main/extension/graph-library.css) gives it margins. On successful toggles, text is briefly inserted and then removed, moving the graph list/workspace vertically. In [`extension/graph-library-page.js`](https://github.com/takahirox/my-audio-to-text/blob/main/extension/graph-library-page.js), `changeVoice()` currently sets: ```js voiceMessage = enabled ? 'Requesting website access…' : 'Turning Web microphone OFF…'; refreshVoiceStatus(); ``` It later clears `voiceMessage` on success. That temporary text is not needed: Chrome displays native permission UI when appropriate, and the switch already supports disabled/aria-busy state. The current `changeVoice()` also sets `toggle.checked = false` before either operation, which can momentarily make an ON -> OFF operation appear completed before persistence/reconciliation succeeds. ## Requested change 1. **Do not render any transient status text for normal toggle progress** (remove `Requesting website access…` and `Turning Web microphone OFF…` from the in-flow status area). Successful ON/OFF operations should not create, expand, collapse or otherwise resize the message area. 2. During an in-flight request, retain the **disabled switch** and `aria-busy="true"` semantics so users cannot trigger duplicate actions; visually represent the *last confirmed persisted ON/OFF state* until the operation succeeds or fails, rather than blindly forcing OFF at the beginning. On success show the new ON/OFF state. Keep keyboard focus behavior. 3. On failure, **show a meaningful actionable error**, preserving the existing denial/cancel, missing website access, failed persistence, rollback/stop, stale cross-tab opt-in and unknown-state warnings. Errors must not be suppressed just to prevent layout shift. Any layout expansion for a genuine error or required user action is acceptable. 4. Preserve the useful persistent warning for **no compatible Web voice graphs**, missing website access, and other state requiring action; do not remove it indiscriminately. A valid successful toggle without an actionable warning should leave `#web-voice-status` empty/hidden. 5. Preserve the existing `chrome.permissions.request` call **synchronously within the switch's user gesture**, explicit ON opt-in, site permission requirements, safety rollback and reconciliation, OFF capture cancellation, cross-tab racing behavior, Web Locks, and compatibility with existing permission grants. Do not relocate the permission request behind an asynchronous step. 6. Keep Graph Library layout and other controls unchanged. Avoid a permanent reserved blank status area solely to conceal an unnecessary progress message, and do not add replacement toasts/popups/spinners with their own layout shifts. ## Acceptance criteria - [ ] Successful Web microphone ON and OFF toggles display **no temporary progress text** in the library, and the graph list/header area does **not jump vertically** as the operation proceeds or completes. - [ ] Switch remains reliably disabled/`aria-busy` while pending; no misleading intermediate OFF state is displayed on an ON -> OFF transition; the final switch/ON–OFF label matches the actual confirmed saved setting. - [ ] Chrome's native host-permission prompt continues to work from a genuine user gesture. A permission denial/dismissal and any save/reconcile failure display useful actionable guidance and leave a safe, consistent state. - [ ] Existing cross-tab toggling and permission-revocation race protections remain intact. - [ ] Missing website permission and no-compatible-graph messaging still appears when relevant; no-error success has an empty/hidden status region. - [ ] Keyboard/screen-reader status and focus behavior remain usable. No change to graph data, graph execution, capture behavior, or the permission scope. ## Tests - Update [`tests/extension/web-voice.spec.js`](https://github.com/takahirox/my-audio-to-text/blob/main/tests/extension/web-voice.spec.js). The existing test for a delayed permission grant around the Web microphone toggle asserts the transient `Requesting website access` text; replace it with assertions for **no transient status**, a busy/disabled switch, accurate confirmed switch state, and stable geometry of the graph list/workspace across the pending-successful transition. - Test normal successful ON and OFF, delayed permission grant, denial, save/reconcile error, concurrent Library ON/OFF, revoked access during a request, and retained actionable warnings. Preserve existing safety-focused test coverage rather than deleting those tests. - Run relevant extension tests and report results in the implementation PR. No performance benchmarks are required. ## Scope Focused UI/feedback cleanup only. Do **not** remove the Web microphone toggle, its separate **ⓘ Website access and microphone help**, the native Chrome access prompt, or real warning/error reporting.
